prompts.title: Scent page
prompts.summary: Describes one scent so a shopper can almost smell it: a place, a moment and the notes.
prompts.prompt:
Write the product page for [scent name] from [shop], a hand-poured [wax] candle.

Notes: top [ ], middle [ ], base [ ]. Size and burn time: [ ]. Price: [ ].

Give: a name line, two sentences that put the scent in a real place and moment (a kitchen in October, a cabin after rain), the notes in plain words, how it burns, and care in one line. No health or aromatherapy claims.
prompts.use: One per scent. Read it out loud; if it sounds like a perfume ad, cut a line.

prompts.title: Wholesale pitch to a local shop
prompts.summary: A short, honest note to a gift shop or boutique asking if they'd carry your candles.
prompts.prompt: Write a short email to [shop name], a [kind of shop] in [town], asking if they'd carry candles from [my shop]. What I know about them: [something true you noticed]. My wholesale terms: [price per candle, minimum order]. Keep it under 120 words, one question at the end, no pressure. Add my name, business and mailing address at the bottom and a line that says if it's a no, I won't write again.
prompts.use: Send one at a time, to shops you'd actually want to be in.

prompts.title: Batch cost check
prompts.summary: Works out what one candle costs you and what the price leaves for your time.
prompts.prompt: Help me price my candles. One batch makes [n] candles. Costs per batch: wax [$], fragrance oil [$], wicks [$], vessels [$], labels [$], packaging [$]. Pouring and curing take me [hours]. Show the cost per candle, what's left at [retail price] and at [wholesale price], and the price where my time is paid at [$ per hour]. Show the math in a table.
prompts.use: Run it every time a supplier price changes.
